verdict_reason: B1 (the r1 production blocker) is genuinely FIXED on all notification paths. But W1's claimed fix is verifiably INERT: the review form's _focus_seconds is never populated by client JS (reference_form.js bails on the review page; onSubmit binds only .ref-question forms), so focus_seconds_reported is still always 0 in production - the exact r1 defect - and the new flow test masks it by POSTing 240 directly, bypassing the broken client. In a fix-audit, a claimed fix that is inert AND concealed by a bypass test is a must-resolve (it defeats the round's contract and would ship a known-broken fraud signal with a misleading test). Promoted to round-2 blocker B2-r2. The JS wiring is small and well-scoped.

findings.title: W1 fix is INERT: the review form's _focus_seconds is never populated by client JS - focus_seconds_reported is still always 0 in production (still present since r1), and the flow test masks it by POSTing 240 directly
findings.evidence: form_pages.gleam view_review renders: html.input([attribute.type_("hidden"), attribute.name("_focus_seconds"), attribute.value("0"), attribute("data-focus-seconds", "")]) inside the reference-review-form. reference_form.js initBrowser: 'var page = doc.querySelector("[data-testid=\'reference-form-page\']"); if (!page) return;' - the review page has data-testid="reference-review", so page is null and initBrowser early-returns. onSubmit (the only writer of [data-focus-seconds]) is attached only via 'questions.forEach(function (section) { var form = section.querySelector("form"); if (form) form.addEventListener("submit", onSubmit); })' - i.e. only to forms inside .ref-question sections; the review form is not one. The flow test focus_seconds_reported_flows_into_the_result_test POSTs '#("_focus_seconds", "240")' via simulate.form_body, never invoking the browser JS.
findings.detail: The r1 W1 defect (focus_seconds_reported structurally always 0) is NOT fixed: the HTML field was added but no client code populates it on the review page, so real browsers still submit the hardcoded 0. The new flow test bypasses the browser, masking the persistence.
findings.recommended_fix: In reference_form.js, attach a submit listener to [data-testid='reference-review-form'] that sets its [data-focus-seconds] field from the running focus accumulator (hoist currentFocusSeconds above the .ref-question bail, persist across review navigation e.g. via sessionStorage), without preventDefault (native POST must proceed). Extend the node --test wiring seam to cover it.

findings.title: B1 fix leaves a dead https:// CTA for the localhost origin_domain (dev-only corner; production unaffected)
findings.evidence: build_entity_url hardcodes '"https://" <> domain <> path'. validate_origin_domain maps localhost -> "localhost:4000" (stored as origin_domain). origin_from_domain("localhost:4000") -> "http://localhost:4000" (invite base_url, correct). So in dev the terminal-notification CTA is https://localhost:4000/... (dead against the http server) while the invite email link is http://localhost:4000/... (works).
findings.detail: Dev-only: production origin_domain is always righttenantry.ie -> https://righttenantry.ie/... (correct). Only a dev testing terminal notifications clicks a dead https://localhost link.
findings.recommended_fix: Special-case localhost/127.0.0.1 in build_entity_url to http:// (mirroring origin_from_domain), or document the dev-only divergence.

findings.title: build_entity_url interpolates the raw origin_domain with zero checks - safe today (write-time allow-list) but no interpolation-time guard for future writers
findings.evidence: build_entity_url: 'let domain = case origin_domain { "" -> "righttenantry.ie" d -> d }; "https://" <> domain <> path'. origin_domain's only writer is validate_origin_domain (allow-list: righttenantry.ie / localhost / *.run.app). The path is fixed UUIDs; the URL is escape_html'd and never fetched server-side.
findings.detail: No open-redirect/SSRF today. But a future writer (backfill/admin/import) storing a crafted domain would silently ship phishing CTAs in landlord emails.
findings.recommended_fix: Defense in depth: validate the domain against the allow-list inside build_entity_url (or a shared helper) at interpolation time.

findings.title: N3 objected-routing branch matches the raw row.status string instead of the typed status_from_string parser classify_row uses in the same file
findings.evidence: Inside the Declined classify arm: 'case row.status { "objected" -> form_pages.view_objected() ...; _ -> form_pages.view_declined() ... }'. classify_row (line 1444) uses 'status: reference_call.status_from_string(row.status)'.
findings.detail: Functionally safe (the Declined arm admits only refused/objected, so the _ fallback is correct). But the branch re-opens the raw DB string after classify_row already parsed it, adding a second untyped status-to-view mapping beside the typed parser.
findings.recommended_fix: Match reference_call.status_from_string(row.status) { Objected -> view_objected; _ -> view_declined } - identical behavior through one typed mapping.

findings.title: B1 fix has no test pin - the exact https://https:// CTA bug would regress silently; notification tests assert type/body only
findings.evidence: build_entity_url is the function B1 fixed; grep of server/test for build_entity_url: 0 matches. The new notification tests assert notification_type + body copy, not the CTA URL (which lives in the Resend payload).
findings.detail: Coverage NONE for B1's regression. Code-level fix verified by reading; risk low (email payload not testable without an SMTP mock). A revert to origin_from_domain would pass every delta test.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a unit test on build_entity_url with a raw origin_domain input asserting a single-scheme URL.

findings.title: W2 decline_reason truncation has no test pin - no test POSTs a >200-char reason; slice(0,200) is code-verified only
findings.evidence: apply_decline: 'application_handler.get_form_value(values, "decline_reason") |> string.slice(0, 200)'. grep of server/test for decline_reason in a long-form POST: 0 matches; existing decline tests send short/no reasons.
findings.detail: Coverage NONE for W2. A crafted long reason would fail closed (untruncated persisted) without a test catching it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add one integration assertion: POST /decline with a 250-char reason; assert stored result->>'decline_reason' is 200 chars.
